answer: Probably yes: a meteg on the first nun (נֵ), to the left of its tsere. Host letter: first nun. Vowel: tsere. I'm not sure enough to resolve this.
visible_evidence: The word מלפנינו is complete in the image and its lower points are visible. Reading right to left under the word: two vertical dots under the lamed (sheva). Then a T/ד-shaped mark under the left part of the pe (kamatz). Then two side-by-side dots under the first nun (tsere). Right after the tsere, to its left, is a separate short vertical stroke with a slight top tick that reaches lower than the dots. Its position, left of the tsere and still under the first nun, matches a meteg. Two things keep confidence below high. First, at this resolution the stroke's top tick makes it look a little like a ן, so I can't fully rule out that it belongs to the kamatz/tsere group or is a print artifact. Second, the kamatz's own stem is drawn off-centre, which could make the marks harder to tell apart. Nothing else under the pe, the second nun or the vav looks like a meteg. The next line's ink is separate and lower down.
